title: Amnesty law agreed with Catalan pro-independence parties in exchange for investiture support
description: To secure re-election as President in November 2023 after finishing second in the July 2023 election, Sánchez agreed with ERC (2 November 2023) and Junts (9 November 2023) to pass an amnesty for acts linked to the Catalan independence process. The deals prompted nightly protests outside PSOE headquarters in Madrid's Calle Ferraz and a mass rally on 18 November 2023 (170,000 people according to the government delegation; about one million according to organisers); the PP and Vox opposed it as a breach of equality before the law, while the government presented it as a step towards normalisation in Catalonia. Ley Orgánica 1/2024 was upheld in its essentials by the Constitutional Court in June 2025 and, according to Spanish press reports, by the Court of Justice of the EU in July 2026; on 6 October 2026, after a Constitutional Court ruling that the amnesty covers malversación, Supreme Court judge Pablo Llarena lifted the arrest warrants against Carles Puigdemont and other former Catalan leaders.
key_facts: 16 November 2023: investiture won by 179 votes to 171 with the votes of ERC and Junts.
30 May 2024: final approval in Congress (177–172); in force on 11 June 2024.
26 June 2025: Constitutional Court ruling STC 137/2025 upheld the law by 6 votes to 4.
16 July 2026: CJEU found the law largely compatible with EU law (press reports).
6 October 2026: arrest warrants against Puigdemont lifted after a Constitutional Court ruling on embezzlement.

title: Five-day pause to consider resigning after the investigation of his wife became public
description: On 24 April 2024, the day it became public that a Madrid court had opened an investigation into his wife Begoña Gómez following a complaint by Manos Limpias, Sánchez published a letter to citizens announcing that he was cancelling his public agenda to consider whether to remain in office, describing the case as part of a campaign of harassment. After a PSOE rally in his support on 27 April, he announced in an institutional statement on 29 April 2024 that he would stay on. Supporters saw a defence against 'lawfare'; opposition parties described the episode as a political manoeuvre and as pressure on the judiciary.
key_facts: 24 April 2024: letter to citizens announcing a period of reflection.
27 April 2024: PSOE gathering in Madrid in his support.
29 April 2024: institutional statement at La Moncloa announcing he would continue.

title: Corruption cases involving two successive PSOE Secretaries of Organisation
description: José Luis Ábalos, Sánchez's Transport Minister and PSOE Secretary of Organisation until 2021, and Santos Cerdán, who held the same party post until June 2025, became the subject of criminal proceedings (see justice records). After a Guardia Civil report on Cerdán was made public on 12 June 2025, Sánchez apologised publicly and said he had been wrong to trust him; on 9 July 2025 he told Congress he had considered but rejected resigning or calling an election, and presented a 15-point State anti-corruption plan, including an independent public-integrity agency and random checks on senior officials' assets. On 22 June 2026 the Supreme Court sentenced Ábalos to 24 years and 3 months in prison. Opposition parties called for his resignation and early elections; Sánchez denied any irregular financing of the PSOE before the Senate inquiry committee on 30 October 2025.
key_facts: 12 June 2025: Cerdán resigned his party posts after the UCO report; Sánchez apologised.
9 July 2025: appearance in Congress and presentation of a 15-measure anti-corruption plan.
30 October 2025: appearance before the Senate committee of inquiry on the Koldo case.
22 June 2026: Supreme Court convicted Ábalos and Koldo García; Sánchez himself is not investigated.

title: Governing without new General State Budgets for the whole 2023–2026 term
description: No new General State Budget (Presupuestos Generales del Estado) was approved during Sánchez's third term: the 2023 budget (Ley 31/2022) was rolled over for 2024, 2025 and 2026. The 2024 budget was abandoned in March 2024 when the Catalan election was called, Congress rejected the deficit and spending targets in July 2024 and again in December 2025, and the 2026 budget was shelved in March 2026. Article 134.3 of the Constitution requires the government to present a budget each year; opposition parties argued that governing without budgets showed the lack of a parliamentary majority, while the government relied on extended budgets and decree-laws.
key_facts: Last approved budget: Ley 31/2022 for 2023 (BOE 24 December 2022).
13 March 2024: the 2024 budget was dropped after the Catalan snap election was called.
July 2024 and 11 December 2025: Congress rejected the stability targets / spending ceiling.
2 January 2026: third consecutive rollover of the 2023 budget.
18 March 2026: the 2026 budget was shelved again.

title: Loss of Junts's support, defeat of the housing decrees and snap election
description: On 27 October 2025 the leadership of Junts per Catalunya decided to break with the PSOE, a decision ratified by 86.98% of its members on 30 October 2025, depriving the government of a stable majority. Several decree-laws were subsequently repealed by Congress, including two housing decree-laws (Real Decreto-ley 26/2026 and 27/2026) on 2 October 2026, with Junts voting alongside the PP and Vox. On 5 October 2026 Sánchez announced the dissolution of the Cortes and a general election for 29 November 2026, about nine months early, saying he needed a broader progressive majority; the government re-issued the housing measures as new decree-laws on 6 October 2026.
key_facts: 30 October 2025: Junts members ratified the break with the PSOE (86.98%).
2 October 2026: Congress repealed Real Decreto-ley 26/2026 on the social function of housing and Real Decreto-ley 27/2026.
5 October 2026: Real Decreto 806/2026 dissolving the Cortes, published in the BOE on 6 October 2026; election on 29 November 2026.

title: Electoral Board sanction proceeding over remarks at a La Moncloa press conference
description: Following complaints by the PP and SALF, the Junta Electoral Central (Central Electoral Board) opened a sanction proceeding (expediente sancionador) against Sánchez on 15 October 2026 over statements at a press conference at La Moncloa on 6 October 2026, the day after the election was called. The Board considered that his remarks on the government's record, housing policy and the opposition 'could have breached' article 50.2 of the electoral law (LOREG) and the duty of neutrality during the electoral period, ordered the Presidency of the Government to remove the statements from its channels and urged him to respect that duty.
key_facts: 6 October 2026: press conference after the Council of Ministers.
15 October 2026: the Junta Electoral Central partly upheld complaints by the PP and SALF and opened a sanction proceeding.
No sanction had been imposed as of 20 October 2026.

title: Shift in Spain's position on Western Sahara
description: In a letter to King Mohammed VI dated 14 March 2022, made public by the Moroccan royal palace on 18 March, Sánchez described Morocco's autonomy plan for Western Sahara as 'the most serious, credible and realistic basis' for resolving the dispute, departing from Spain's long-standing neutrality. The change was made without prior consultation of Parliament or the coalition partner Unidas Podemos, was criticised by most parliamentary groups and led Algeria to recall its ambassador; the government defended it as necessary to restore relations with Morocco after the 2021 Ceuta migration crisis. Sánchez visited Rabat on 7 April 2022.
key_facts: 14 March 2022: letter to Mohammed VI; published by Rabat on 18 March 2022.
Algeria recalled its ambassador to Spain.
7 April 2022: official visit to Morocco to relaunch bilateral relations.

title: Pegasus spyware infection of the President's phone
description: On 2 May 2022 the government announced that the mobile phones of Sánchez and Defence Minister Margarita Robles had been infected in 2021 with the Pegasus spyware, shortly after revelations that pro-independence Catalan politicians had also been targeted. The director of the CNI intelligence service, Paz Esteban, was dismissed on 10 May 2022. The Audiencia Nacional investigation was shelved provisionally in 2023, reopened in April 2024 and shelved again on 22 January 2026 because Israel did not respond to requests for judicial cooperation; no perpetrator has been identified.
key_facts: 2 May 2022: government announcement of the infections.
10 May 2022: dismissal of the CNI director.
22 January 2026: second provisional closure of the case by the Audiencia Nacional (Juzgado Central de Instrucción nº 4).

title: Plagiarism allegations about his doctoral thesis
description: In September 2018 several media outlets, including ABC, alleged that parts of Sánchez's 2012 doctoral thesis at the Universidad Camilo José Cela, and of a related book, contained passages reproduced without proper attribution. Sánchez denied any plagiarism and had the thesis published online together with the results of anti-plagiarism software checks. No formal finding of plagiarism was made, and in February 2019 the Supreme Court rejected a criminal complaint filed by Vox over the thesis, finding no offence.
key_facts: September 2018: allegations published; the thesis was made public together with anti-plagiarism reports.
Part of the allegations concerned a book derived from the thesis rather than the thesis itself.
February 2019: the Supreme Court rejected Vox's criminal complaint.

title: Refusal of NATO's 5% of GDP defence-spending target
description: Ahead of NATO's summit in The Hague on 24–25 June 2025, Sánchez announced that Spain would not commit to spending 5% of GDP on defence and security, saying about 2.1% was sufficient to meet its capability targets, and cited a letter from Secretary General Mark Rutte of 22 June 2025 giving Spain 'flexibility'. The summit declaration does not mention any exemption, and whether Spain obtained one was disputed. US President Donald Trump repeatedly criticised Spain's position, including suggesting in October 2025 that Spain should be expelled from NATO.
key_facts: 22 June 2025: letter from Mark Rutte to Sánchez.
25 June 2025: The Hague Summit Declaration sets the 5% target without naming Spain.
The government states that Spain will spend about 2.1% of GDP on defence.

title: David Sánchez / Diputación de Badajoz case: administrative prevaricación (Audiencia Provincial de Badajoz)
description: Criminal case over the hiring and later change of post of David Sánchez, the President's brother, as head of the performing-arts office (Oficina de Artes Escénicas) of the Badajoz Provincial Council (Diputación de Badajoz), brought by popular accusations including Manos Limpias, HazteOír, the PP and Vox; the public prosecutor did not accuse him. Co-defendants included Miguel Ángel Gallardo, former president of the provincial council and former PSOE leader in Extremadura. On 14 July 2026 the Audiencia Provincial de Badajoz convicted David Sánchez at first instance of administrative prevaricación as a necessary cooperator and acquitted him of influence peddling. Pedro Sánchez is not a party to the case. Outcome so far: First-instance judgment of 14 July 2026: nine years of special disqualification from public employment or office (inhabilitación especial) for David Sánchez, with no prison sentence, and acquittal on the influence-peddling charge; Gallardo received two nine-year disqualifications (for creating the post and for later converting it into head of the performing-arts office). David Sánchez and Gallardo appealed in October 2026 to the High Court of Justice of Extremadura. The judgment is not final. The conviction is not final and is under appeal; David Sánchez and the other defendants remain presumed innocent until a final judgment and deny wrongdoing. The court found no proof that David Sánchez exerted pressure or used his family tie to influence anyone. Pedro Sánchez is not investigated in this case.
key_facts: The public prosecutor sought acquittal of all defendants; the charges were maintained by popular accusations.
Trial held from 28 May to 9 June 2026 after a postponement from February 2026.
14 July 2026: conviction for administrative prevaricación (nine years' disqualification), linked by the court to the 2022 change to his post; acquittal for influence peddling.
Gallardo received two nine-year disqualifications and nine other defendants nine years each.
October 2026: appeals filed before the TSJ de Extremadura.

title: Koldo case, face-mask contracts: José Luis Ábalos, Koldo García and Víctor de Aldama (Tribunal Supremo)
description: Supreme Court case against José Luis Ábalos, Sánchez's Minister of Transport (2018–2021) and former PSOE Secretary of Organisation, his former adviser Koldo García and businessman Víctor de Aldama over contracts for face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic and related payments. After his indictment in November 2025, Ábalos was remanded in custody on 27 November 2025. On 22 June 2026 the Supreme Court convicted Ábalos and García of criminal organisation, bribery (cohecho), misuse of public funds and influence peddling. Pedro Sánchez is not a party to the case. Outcome so far: Unanimous Supreme Court judgment notified on 22 June 2026: Ábalos 24 years and 3 months in prison; Koldo García 19 years, 8 months and 1 day; Aldama 4 years and 6 months, suspended in view of his cooperation with the justice system. On 14 October 2026 the Supreme Court rejected the defendants' requests to annul the judgment; an appeal for constitutional protection (amparo) before the Constitutional Court remains possible. Ábalos and Koldo García have been convicted by the Supreme Court, Spain's highest ordinary court; they deny the offences and may seek amparo before the Constitutional Court. Pedro Sánchez is not investigated in this case.
key_facts: 3 November 2025: Ábalos, García and Aldama formally indicted (procesamiento).
27 November 2025: Ábalos and García remanded in custody without bail for flight risk.
7 April – 6 May 2026: trial before seven judges of the Supreme Court.
22 June 2026: unanimous conviction (ECLI:ES:TS:2026:2553).
14 October 2026: requests to annul the judgment rejected.

title: Public-works contracts investigation: Santos Cerdán, Ábalos, Koldo García and others (Audiencia Nacional)
description: Investigation into alleged kickbacks on public-works contracts, based on a Guardia Civil (UCO) report made public on 12 June 2025, involving Santos Cerdán, PSOE Secretary of Organisation until June 2025, as well as Ábalos, Koldo García, Aldama and former executives of the construction group Acciona. Cerdán resigned his party posts and his seat in June 2025, was remanded in custody from 30 June to 19 November 2025 and released with precautionary measures. After Ábalos gave up his parliamentary seat, the Supreme Court transferred the investigation to the Audiencia Nacional on 2 February 2026. Pedro Sánchez is not investigated. Investigation stage: Santos Cerdán and the other suspects have not been tried or convicted and are presumed innocent; they deny the allegations. Pedro Sánchez is not under investigation.
key_facts: 12 June 2025: UCO report made public; Sánchez publicly apologised and Cerdán resigned his PSOE posts.
30 June 2025: Cerdán remanded in custody; released on 19 November 2025 with periodic court appearances and a travel ban.
2 February 2026: the Supreme Court declared it no longer had jurisdiction and sent the case to the Audiencia Nacional.
No indictment for trial as of October 2026.

title: Investigation into PSOE cash payments (Audiencia Nacional)
description: Separate line of investigation opened in November 2025 at the Audiencia Nacional, at the request of Supreme Court judge Leopoldo Puente, into cash payments made by the PSOE to party officials between 2017 and 2024. The judge ordered the party to report all such payments, including any made to Sánchez, and the PSOE handed over the documentation in December 2025, after which the line was placed under secrecy. Before the Senate inquiry committee on 30 October 2025, Sánchez said he may have settled expenses in cash against invoices, denied ever receiving more than 1,000 euros in an envelope, and described the party's financing as legal. Secret investigation stage; neither the PSOE as an organisation nor Pedro Sánchez is under investigation, and no charges have been brought. Any irregularity remains unproven.
key_facts: 6 November 2025: separate line (pieza separada) opened.
3 December 2025: the judge ordered the PSOE to report cash payments from 2017–2024, including any to Sánchez.
17 December 2025: the line was placed under secrecy.
30 October 2025: Sánchez told the Senate committee that cash settlement of expenses against invoices was normal practice 'within the limits of legality'.

title: Leire Díez case: alleged efforts to obstruct investigations, and SEPI contracts (Audiencia Nacional)
description: Investigation into Leire Díez, a PSOE member described in the press as the party's 'fontanera' (plumber), after recordings published in May 2025 suggested attempts to gather compromising information on Guardia Civil investigators and prosecutors working on cases affecting the PSOE, and into alleged kickbacks on contracts at the state holding company SEPI. Santos Cerdán and PSOE manager Ana Fuentes were among those named as suspects in May 2026. Since August 2026 the case has been handled by Audiencia Nacional judge Santiago Pedraz, who on 9 October 2026 refused 'for now' the PP's request to investigate the PSOE as a legal entity. Pedro Sánchez is not investigated. Investigation stage: Leire Díez and the other suspects have not been charged for trial or convicted and are presumed innocent. The PSOE is not under investigation as an organisation and Pedro Sánchez is not a suspect.
key_facts: July 2025: a Madrid court opened an inquiry for alleged influence peddling, bribery and obstruction of justice.
December 2025: Díez arrested together with a former SEPI president and a businessman in the SEPI contracts investigation.
27 May 2026: Cerdán, Ana Fuentes and Gaspar Zarrías named as suspects.
9 October 2026: Judge Pedraz rejected, for now, the PP's request to investigate the PSOE as a legal person.

title: Former Attorney General Álvaro García Ortiz: revelation of confidential information (Tribunal Supremo)
description: Trial of Álvaro García Ortiz, Attorney General (Fiscal General del Estado) appointed on the proposal of Sánchez's government, over the leak of confidential information concerning Alberto González Amador, the partner of Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso, who was under investigation for tax fraud. On 20 November 2025 the Supreme Court convicted him by five votes to two. Pedro Sánchez is not a party to the case. Outcome so far: Supreme Court judgment (verdict 20 November 2025, full text 9 December 2025): two years' disqualification from the office of Attorney General, a fine of 7,200 euros and 10,000 euros in compensation. García Ortiz left office and was replaced by Teresa Peramato in December 2025. In April 2026 the public prosecution service and García Ortiz filed amparo appeals before the Constitutional Court, pending as of October 2026; on 11 June 2026 the Supreme Court reported against a pardon. García Ortiz has been convicted by the Supreme Court; he maintains his innocence and has sought amparo before the Constitutional Court. Pedro Sánchez is not a party to this case.
key_facts: 16 October 2024: the Supreme Court opened proceedings against the Attorney General.
3–13 November 2025: trial.
20 November 2025: conviction by 5 votes to 2 for revelation of confidential information.
April 2026: amparo appeals filed with the Constitutional Court.
